title: Length-distribution sampler and kernel-affinity matcher
body:
Purpose and quick summary:

This note captures a working design for a low-cost, low-latency strategy that: 1) continuously samples the recent request length distribution, 2) derives micro-buckets and an expected packing mix, and 3) selects a kernel profile + KV warmstart strategy per-batch using a kernel-affinity score. The intent is pragmatic: small implementation surface, measurable cost wins, and safe quality guardrails.

Background / motivation:
- Production traces show a heavy head (~short prompts < 32 tokens) and a long tail (occasional > 2k tokens). Static fixed-pad policies waste GPU cycles and reduce throughput. Existing bucketers either over-fragment (too many tiny kernels) or over-pad (big waste).
- We want an adaptive layer that reacts to moment-to-moment len distribution changes (e.g., promotions, new customer flows) without expensive global re-profiling.
- Also needs to coordinate with KV cache warmup: when coalescing similar prefixes, pre-warm the KV shards to avoid cold-start latency spikes.

Design goals / acceptance criteria:
- Improve average token cost by >= 8% vs current fixed-pad baseline on typical traces.
- P99 tail latency must not increase by > 5% absolute.
- Perceptual quality regressions (measured by eval prompt sets) limited to delta-perplexity <= 0.8 and human spot checks pass.
- Implementable as a lightweight runtime shim (no model changes).

Core components (high level):
1) Reservoir-length sampler (RLS)
   - Continuous reservoir sampling of request sequence lengths (tokens) over sliding window W (default W = 10k requests, decay half-life = 30m).
   - Store (len, timestamp, route-id) tuples. Prefer modest memory (< 64k entries).
   - Periodically (every T = 10s) compute histogram H over lengths, with exponential decay on older samples.

2) Micro-bucket generator
   - From H, derive a small set of micro-buckets B = {b1..bN} where N is 4-8 (adaptive).
   - Algorithm: find modes and knee points using a smoothed derivative on H; collapse adjacent low-pop buckets; ensure coverage of 90-95% of mass with N <= 8.
   - Each bucket stores: bucket_id, target_len (representative), probability mass p_b.

3) Kernel-affinity scorer (KAS)
   - For each kernel variant k (e.g., small-seq fast-kernel, long-seq tiled-kernel, quantized-8b-kernel), maintain a small profile: latency_base(ms), per_token(ms), memory_headroom, supports_kv_segmented (bool), warmstart_penalty(ms).
   - Compute affinity score for bucket b to kernel k: score(b,k) = alpha * est_latency(b,k) + beta * est_cost(b,k) + gamma * warmstart_impact(b,k) + delta * reliability_penalty(k).
   - Normalization: lower score = preferred. Tunable weights (alpha..delta) set by experiments.

4) Packing policy / stochastic trim layer
   - For a target batch, sample the runtime histogram (fast path) and pick top M buckets that cover batch's incoming requests.
   - Two packing actions: coalesce (group by representative length and run fast-kernel with minimal per-item padding) OR trim+coalesce (for very long tails).
   - Stochastic tail-trim: for sequences longer than T_trim (default 1024), with probability p_trim(len) = min(0.2, (len - T_trim) / (3*T_trim)), propose trimming the tail tokens up to trim_amount = min(ceil(0.05 * len), 128). Trim only if model-level guards (prompt eval) passed. Purpose: reduce padding overhead when paired with shorter sequences.

5) KV warmstart fingerprinting
   - When batches coalesce sequences sharing high prefix overlap (estimated by prefix-hash collisions or route-id), emit a warmstart hint for the KV shard(s) that will be touched. The runtime will pre-touch/prepare the relevant KV pages for the target GPU context.
   - Fingerprint: simple 64-bit rolling hash of first 256 tokens or route-id if available. Warmstart is async; we accept ~1-3ms extra cost for pre-warm to reduce p99 tail on coalesced batches.

6) Rollout and safety
   - Start as opt-in per-route via route config (console switch). Canary across 5% traffic with strict SLO monitoring. Auto-disable if p99 latency regresses beyond threshold.

Execution flow (per request batch):
- Ingress collects request lengths and appends to reservoir (fast, lock-free ring).
- On batching decision: fetch current B and kernel affinities. For each candidate kernel, compute expected batch utility (weighted by p_b). Pick kernel with minimal expected score.
- If selected policy includes coalesce+warmstart: calculate fingerprint set, send warmstart async, assemble batch with minimal padding or stochastic-trim applied.
- Emit telemetry: chosen_kernel, chosen_bucket, pad_overhead_tokens, trimmed_tokens, warmstart_requested.

Offline sim / evaluation plan:
- Build a replay harness that consumes production traces (two weeks) and simulates the sampler + bucket generator. Important metrics: avg tokens padded per-batch, GPU utilization, pp-token cost estimate, p50/p95/p99 latency distributions, and model quality deltas on evaluation prompt set.
- Target A/B: 2-week canary on low-risk tenant group; initial traffic 5% then expand.

Telemetry & metrics to add:
- len_sampler.samples_total, reservoir_fill_ratio, bucket_count, bucket_mass_percentiles
- kernel_affinity.{kernel}.score_hist, chosen_kernel.rate
- pad_overhead.tokens.avg / trimmed_tokens.avg
- warmstart.hints.sent / warmstart.hit_rate / warmstart_latency_reduction_ms
- eval.quality.{route}.perplexity.delta (nightly)

Open design questions / tradeoffs:
- Trimming safety: what are model-level guardrails we can apply? We need a small eval set that approximates customer-sensitive completions to test trimming impact. Also consider applying trimming only to non-instruction prompts (heuristic).
- Warmstart cost: pre-touching KV memory can help latency but adds memory churn. Which warmstart window size minimizes net cost?
- Determinism & fairness: stochastic trimming favors short-request latency but may bias some user flows. Consider per-customer rate-limits on trimming.
- How to handle multi-tenant isolation: reservoir should be per-tenant or global? Start global with route-tagging and move to per-tenant for heavy customers.

Implementation timeline / milestones (rough):
- Week 1-2: implement reservoir sampler + histogram builder + unit tests. (owners: Samir, Jon)
- Week 3: micro-bucket algorithm + offline sim harness. Basic metrics & dashboards. (Elena)
- Week 4-5: kernel-affinity scorer and runtime hook + warmstart hint plumbing. Simulate expected cost wins. (Samir)
- Week 6: deploy canary, monitor; roll forward/back.

Small experiments we should run quickly:
- Offline sim: compare baseline fixed-pad(128) vs dynamic micro-buckets on 3 production traces. Target: pad_token_reduction >= 8%.
- Warmstart microbench: measure p99 with and without warmstart on coalesced prefixes (synth workloads).
- Trimming AB: small deterministic trim (always trim 16 tokens for >2048) vs stochastic trim to measure quality delta and padding reduction.

Risks and mitigations:
- Quality regressions from trimming: mitigated by conservative p_trim, route opt-in, and nightly evals.
- Complexity: keep N buckets small; degrade to a safe default (largest-kernel) if sampler fails.
- Telemetry volume: ensure hist updates are aggregated before export.

Appendix: short pseudo-code for sampler + selection (informal)

// reservoir insert (fast)
function add_sample(len, route_id) -> void:
  idx = atomic_inc(reservoir_ptr) % RES_SIZE
  reservoir[idx] = (len, now(), route_id)

// periodic bucket derivation
function derive_buckets() -> list(B):
  H = smoothed_hist(reservoir with decay)
  modes = find_modes(H)
  knees = find_knees(H)
  B = collapse_to_micro_buckets(modes, knees, target_N=6)
  return B

// kernel selection per-batch
function select_kernel(batch_lens):
  B = current_buckets()
  for each kernel k in kernel_profiles:
    exp_score[k] = sum_over_b(p_b * score(b,k))
  return argmin_k(exp_score)

Unresolved TODOs in doc:
- Add concrete weight defaults (alpha..delta) after perf runs.
- Decide per-tenant reservoir scheduling and storage limits.
- Build small "trim-safety" eval set (ask research for curated prompts).

Links & references:

- JIRA ENG-2147: "adaptive len sampler and kernel mapping"
- GH PR: redwood-inference/serving-runtime#4021 (initial sampler impl)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally an exploratory doc; please call out missing perf knobs or safety concerns. If you have strong objections to trimming, say so and include examples we should protect.
- If you have previously instrumented per-route length histograms, point me to the code (I couldn't find a canonical exporter).

Quick contact: ping me (Ava Chen) or drop notes in #serving-runtime.
